definitions.explanation: The direction opposite to south, toward the Arctic in the Northern Hemisphere.

examples.japanese: {北海道|ほっかいどう}は{日本|にほん}の{北|きた}にあります。
examples.english: Hokkaido is in the north of Japan.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{北口|きたぐち}で{待|ま}っています。
examples.english: I'll be waiting at the north exit of the station.

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}を{北|きた}に{歩|ある}くと、{大|おお}きい{公園|こうえん}があります。
examples.english: If you walk north on this road, there's a big park.

notes:
{北|きた} is one of the four cardinal directions in Japanese.

THE FOUR DIRECTIONS:
- {東|ひがし}: east
- {西|にし}: west
- {南|みなみ}: south
- {北|きた}: north

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {北口|きたぐち}: north exit (at stations)
- {北側|きたがわ}: north side
- {北風|きたかぜ}: north wind
- {北海道|ほっかいどう}: Hokkaido ("northern sea road")
- {北極|ほっきょく}: North Pole
- {東北|とうほく}: Tohoku (northeast Japan)

USAGE WITH PARTICLES:
- {北|きた}へ{行|い}く: to go north (direction)
- {北|きた}に{住|す}む: to live in the north (location)
- {北|きた}から{来|く}る: to come from the north (origin)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Station exits in Japan are often labeled by cardinal direction ({北口|きたぐち}, {南口|みなみぐち}, etc.). This is essential for navigating and giving directions.
